drafts.title: Provide longer adjustable thigh support on front seats
drafts.description: Front-seat occupants can adjust the cushion length so tall drivers feel continuous thigh support on long drives and while seated statically.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front-seat cushion offers an adjustable thigh-support extension of at least 60 mm from the retracted position; extension must provide contact with the mid-thigh for drivers up to 195 cm in 95% of ergonomic test postures.
assumptions: 60 mm extension is feasible within current seat packaging for the 5 Series footprint.
Ergonomic test posture refers to standard seating reference points used in vehicle seating validation.
uncertainties: Exact required extension for the tallest subset of users may vary; additional adjustments (tilt/height) could be needed to satisfy all body shapes.
Impact on seat heating/ventilation integration and side-bolster comfort needs verification.

drafts.title: Cup holders sized for common large bottles and travel mugs
drafts.description: Customers can place common 1.0 L bottles and insulated travel mugs in the vehicle cup holders without wobble or needing alternative storage.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At least one front and one rear cup holder accommodates bottles up to 1.0 L (diameter 85 mm, height 300 mm) and travel mugs up to 90 mm diameter while retaining the item during a lateral acceleration of 0.5 g.
assumptions: Common large water bottles and insulated mugs fall within the specified dimensions.
Retention during 0.5 g lateral acceleration is a representative proxy for real-world holding performance.
uncertainties: Very large or unusually shaped bottles may still require alternate storage.
Integration with center console design constraints may limit exact diameter or retention geometry.

drafts.title: Hands-free tailgate opens reliably on first attempt
drafts.description: Customers using the hands-free foot gesture can expect the tailgate to open on the first correct attempt without multiple tries.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Successful opening on the first correct foot gesture in ≥95% of attempts, with the tailgate beginning to open within 3 seconds of the gesture; measured across ambient temperatures from -20°C to +40°C and in wet conditions.
assumptions: ‘Correct foot gesture’ is defined per existing user guidance and is reproducible in user tests.
Environmental ranges (-20°C to +40°C) cover the majority of customer-reported failure conditions.
uncertainties: Edge cases with obstructed sensors, heavy cargo at tailgate edge, or non-standard user gait may still reduce reliability.
Interactions with key fob location and security interlocks may affect perceived responsiveness.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting with expanded color and brightness options
drafts.description: Customers can personalize interior ambient lighting with many distinct colors and fine-grained brightness control across multiple zones.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: System offers at least 64 distinct color choices and at least 10 discrete brightness levels (including off) per zone, with individually adjustable control for a minimum of 4 cabin zones (e.g., front doors, rear doors, dashboard, center console).
assumptions: 64 distinct colors are perceivable as meaningfully different by users under typical cabin lighting.
Four zones covers the majority of personalization needs expressed by customers.
uncertainties: Some customers may expect dynamic color gradients or app-based color selection beyond discrete colors.
Power consumption and visibility under very bright daylight need verification for perceived brightness steps.

drafts.title: Seat memory restores saved positions reliably and quickly
drafts.description: When a customer recalls a saved seat memory, the seat returns to the saved position consistently and within a short time so drivers don't need manual re-adjustment.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Saved seat position is restored within ±15 mm fore/aft and ±2° backrest angle in ≥98% of restores across 50 consecutive cycles, and the restore completes within 5 seconds.
assumptions: Measurement tolerances reference standard seat position points used in seating validation.
50-cycle test across representative temperature range is a valid reliability indicator.
uncertainties: Memory interaction with multi-user profiles, steering-wheel and mirror positions may introduce additional restore variance.
Mechanical wear or battery state in remote fobs may affect real-world restore rates.

drafts.title: Door handles operate reliably in freezing/weather exposure
drafts.description: Customers can open flush door handles in freezing weather without manual de-icing or repeated attempts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Handles allow opening on first user attempt in ≥98% of cases after exposure to -20°C ambient with up to 5 mm surface ice accretion in a standardized freeze test, without requiring manual scraping or interior unlocking sequences.
assumptions: Standardized freeze test (temperature, ice thickness) represents common winter extremes reported by customers.
Solutions may include mechanical, sealing, or thermal strategies as long as customer outcome is met.
uncertainties: Extreme conditions beyond test parameters (e.g., salt contamination, thicker ice) may still affect operation.
Long-term durability of any anti-freeze measures needs validation.

drafts.title: Rear legroom at least as generous as main competitors
drafts.description: Rear-seat passengers experience legroom equal to or exceeding the main competitors so that taller passengers are not cramped.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Rear knee clearance (knee point to front seat back) ≥980 mm when front seats set to standard reference positions, measured per standard vehicle seating measurement method.
assumptions: 980 mm is a reasonable target to match or exceed the main competitors in the segment at successor launch.
Measurement uses an agreed vehicle seating standard so values are comparable to competitor data.
uncertainties: Exact competitor values may change before successor launch; packaging trade-offs (battery, hybrid components) may constrain available legroom.
Meeting this may require compromises in front-seat adjustability or interior packaging.

drafts.title: Provide a trunk power outlet usable for portable coolers
drafts.description: Customers can power a portable cooler directly from the trunk without adapters or external batteries.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At least one easily accessible power outlet in the trunk that can supply power continuously for portable coolers up to 120 W; outlet placement allows standard cooler cables to reach typical trunk floor positions.
assumptions: 120 W continuous draw covers the majority of consumer portable coolers.
Outlet availability while vehicle is parked (accessory power mode) is acceptable to customers.
uncertainties: Vehicle electrical system constraints or regulations may limit continuous power availability in some markets.
Exact outlet type/connector preferences vary by region.

drafts.title: Request for 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder for the volume knob (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers asked explicitly for a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder to be used in the volume knob.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Engineering specification request: use a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder for the volume control.
assumptions: This is a component-level request rather than a direct customer-facing outcome.
uncertainties: Implementation may be constrained by supplier availability, cost, or integration with the HMI system.
drafts.scope_reason: This is an explicit component engineering specification (part-level). Requirements for successor must be customer-facing; engineering part choices are out of scope.

drafts.title: Request for 4.5 mm laminated side windows (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers asked that side windows use 4.5 mm thick laminated glass.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Engineering specification request: laminated glass, 4.5 mm thickness for side windows.
assumptions: This is a material/thickness specification rather than a defined customer experience.
uncertainties: Trade-offs include weight, cost, NVH performance and regulatory glass requirements by market.
drafts.scope_reason: This is an explicit engineering/material specification; customer-facing outcomes (e.g., quieter cabin) should be specified instead for in-scope requirements.

drafts.title: Request for seat cushion foam density of 55 kg/m³ (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers asked specifically for seat cushion foam with a density of 55 kg per cubic meter.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Engineering specification request: seat-cushion foam density = 55 kg/m³.
assumptions: This is a material-level request expressing a perceived comfort preference.
uncertainties: Comfort perception depends on foam formulation, layering and cover materials, not density alone.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific material-property requests are engineering specifications; convert to customer-facing comfort targets for in-scope requirements.

drafts.title: Request that the front end meets EU pedestrian protection regulation (regulation request)
drafts.description: Customers requested that the vehicle front end complies with the new EU pedestrian protection rules.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: front-end design to meet the referenced EU pedestrian protection regulation.
assumptions: This signal cites a regulation requirement rather than a customer-experience specification.
uncertainties: Regulatory requirements and their timelines may change; engineering trade-offs may be required to meet the regulation in all markets.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/homologation requests are out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Request that rear-seat airbags obtain FMVSS 208 certification (regulation request)
drafts.description: Customers asked that rear-seat airbags meet FMVSS 208 certification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: rear-seat airbag system to achieve FMVSS 208 certification.
assumptions: This is a regulatory/certification ask rather than a direct customer experience description.
uncertainties: Certification processes differ by market and may impose design constraints; feasibility depends on regulatory timelines.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/certification requests are out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request that headlights follow ECE R112 beam pattern rules in every market (regulation request)
drafts.description: Customers asked for headlights to follow the ECE R112 beam pattern rules across markets.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: headlights conform to ECE R112 beam pattern requirements.
assumptions: This request references a regulatory beam-pattern standard rather than a direct customer-experience target.
uncertainties: Headlight system variants and market homologation differences may require multiple technical solutions.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/homologation requests are out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Request for BMW to guarantee a 60% residual value after five years (financial guarantee request)
drafts.description: Customers requested a BMW-backed guarantee of a 60% residual value after five years.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: BMW guarantee of 60% residual value after five years.
assumptions: This is a financial/ownership guarantee request rather than a product feature.
uncertainties: Residual-value guarantees involve business models and risk management outside product requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Price, residual-value guarantees and financial commitments are out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: Request that BMW cuts production cost per car by 8% (business target request)
drafts.description: Customers asked that BMW reduce production cost per car by 8%.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: production cost reduction of 8% per car.
assumptions: This is a corporate cost target rather than a customer-facing capability.
uncertainties: Production-cost targets are organizational/business decisions not appropriate as product requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Business/production cost targets are out of scope for product requirements.
